title: Unable to Call functions in Java Plugins - JNI Android
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in:
Godot 4.4.1 mono stable
Godot 4.5dev3 mono
Godot 4.5dev4 mono
Godot v4.3.stable.mono.flathub

### System information

Debian (trixie)

### Issue description

Godot seems to have an issue with Java plugin integration on Android.

Java Plugins that are apparently correctly Built, 
and correctly included on the final Android Build > cannot be Called from inside Godot.

The plugins are correctly built with Gradle, included in the Android export, and recognized as Singletons, 
but their @UsedByGodot-annotated methods/functions (helloWorld, getPluginName, checkConnection) are not detected or Callable; this makes working on/with such plugins impossible.

This problem affects both custom made Plugins like and AudioCapture plugin I'm trying to develop.
But also third-party solution, like this Godot-Android-Plugin-Template in Github:
https://github.com/m4gr3d/Godot-Android-Plugin-Template

This indicates a flaw in Godot’s Java plugin system. 

This issue persists across Godot 4.5.dev3 and 4.5.dev4, with fresh Export Templates.

I have posted a thread on the Godot Forum where all details can be found:
https://forum.godotengine.org/t/unable-to-call-functions-in-java-plugin-java-jni-android/110845

But I'm tryin to summarize it here, based on the result I got with Godot-Android-Plugin-Template,
which can serve as a common ground for confirmation, or to make a solution..

### Steps to reproduce

- Download the Godot-Android-Plugin-Template:
https://github.com/m4gr3d/Godot-Android-Plugin-Template

- Update build.gradle.kts:
jvmTarget = "17"
compileSdk = 34
implementation("org.godotengine:godot:4.4.1.stable")

- Update gradle-wrapper.properties to use gradle-8.2-bin.zip.

- Set rootProject.name = "JavaTemplateTest" in settings.gradle.kts.

- Update export_plugin.gd and plugin.cfg to use name="JavaTemplateTest".

Place plugin files in addons/JavaTemplateTest with the structure: 
```
addons/JavaTemplateTest/
├── bin/
│   ├── debug/
│   │   └── JavaTemplateTest-debug.aar
│   └── release/
│       └── JavaTemplateTest-release.aar
├── export_plugin.gd
└── plugin.cfg
```

- Build and Run:
Build the plugin from it's root folder, with Gradle (./gradlew assemble).

- Configure Godot Project:
Use Godot 4.5.dev3 or 4.5.dev4 (Mono).
Enable the JavaTemplateTest plugin in Project Settings > Plugins.

Add basic GDscript code/functions to check and call the plugin:
```
var _template_plugin_name = "JavaTemplateTest"
var _template_android_plugin_instance = null

func _ready():
    if OS.get_name() == "Android":
        if Engine.has_singleton(_template_plugin_name):
            _template_android_plugin_instance = Engine.get_singleton(_template_plugin_name)
            if is_instance_valid(_template_android_plugin_instance):
                print("Template plugin '", _template_plugin_name, "' instance obtained: ", _template_android_plugin_instance)
                call_template_plugin_test_method()
            else:
                printerr("Failed to get valid instance for '", _template_plugin_name, "'.")
        else:
            printerr("Couldn't find plugin '", _template_plugin_name, "'.")
    ....
    template_test() #just a raw call
    call_template_plugin_test_method()

func template_test():
	if _android_plugin:
		print("Attempting to call helloWorld() on template plugin...")
		_android_plugin.helloWorld() # This is the actual call
		print("Called helloWorld(). Check for Toast and logcat.")
	else:
		printerr("Template plugin instance not available to call helloWorld().")

func call_template_plugin_test_method(): # Renamed for clarity
	if is_instance_valid(_template_android_plugin_instance): # Check validity again before use
		print("Attempting to call helloWorld() on template plugin '", _template_plugin_name, "'...")
		var method_to_call = "helloWorld" # Exact Java/Kotlin method name
		if _template_android_plugin_instance.has_method(method_to_call):
			_template_android_plugin_instance.helloWorld() # This is the actual call
			print("Called helloWorld() on template plugin. Check for Toast and logcat.")
		else:
			printerr("Template plugin '", _template_plugin_name, "' instance does NOT have method '", method_to_call, "'.")
	else:
		printerr("Template plugin '", _template_plugin_name, "' instance not available or invalid to call helloWorld().")
```

Configure the plugin for Android export in export_plugin.gd:
```
@tool
extends EditorPlugin
var export_plugin : AndroidExportPlugin

func _enter_tree():
	# Initialization of the plugin goes here.
	export_plugin = AndroidExportPlugin.new()
	add_export_plugin(export_plugin)

func _exit_tree():
	# Clean-up of the plugin goes here.
	remove_export_plugin(export_plugin)
	export_plugin = null

class AndroidExportPlugin extends EditorExportPlugin:
	var _plugin_name = "JavaTemplateTest" # This still needs to match your plugin.cfg 'name' for singleton lookup

	func _supports_platform(platform):
		if platform is EditorExportPlatformAndroid:
			return true
		return false

	func _get_android_libraries(platform, debug):
		if debug:			
			return PackedStringArray(["../addons/JavaTemplateTest/bin/debug/JavaTemplateTest-debug.aar"])
		else:
			return PackedStringArray(["../addons/JavaTemplateTest/bin/release/JavaTemplateTest-release.aar"])

	func _get_android_dependencies(platform, debug):
		# No Maven dependencies for this template plugin itself
		return PackedStringArray([])

	func _get_name():
		return _plugin_name
		return "JavaTemplateTestExportScript" # Or keep as _plugin_name, it's less critical
```

Export the Godot project to Android using a fresh export template. 
Run on an Android device

Result:
Godot log shows the plugin Exists, and is Loaded as a JNI singleton:
Template plugin ‘JavaTemplateTest’ instance obtained: <JNISingleton#2734686363>
Attempting to call helloWorld() on template plugin ‘JavaTemplateTest’…
ERROR: Template plugin ‘JavaTemplateTest’ instance does NOT have method ‘helloWorld’.
ERROR: Template plugin instance not available to call helloWorld().
Attempting to call helloWorld() on template plugin ‘JavaTemplateTest’…
ERROR: Template plugin ‘JavaTemplateTest’ instance does NOT have method ‘helloWorld’.

This is the HelloWorld function inside the template plugin:
```
@UsedByGodot
fun helloWorld() {
runOnUiThread {
Toast.makeText(activity, “Hello World”, Toast.LENGTH_LONG).show()
Log.v(pluginName, “Hello World”)
```

The most basic functions are not callable…

**Alternative**
Custom Plugin:
Create a custom Java plugin (e.g., TestPluginName) with methods:
```
package org.godotengine.plugin.android.template

import android.util.Log
import android.widget.Toast
import org.godotengine.godot.Godot
import org.godotengine.godot.plugin.GodotPlugin
import org.godotengine.godot.plugin.UsedByGodot

class GodotAndroidPlugin(godot: Godot): GodotPlugin(godot) {
    override fun getPluginName() = BuildConfig.GODOT_PLUGIN_NAME
  
    @UsedByGodot
    public String checkConnection() {
        Log.i(TAG, "Minimal Java checkConnection() method successfully called from GDScript!");
        return "Minimal Java plugin is connected and responding!";
    }    
}
```

Build with Gradle using the template extracted from android_source.zip:
```
dependencies {
    compileOnly files('libs/godot-lib.template_release.aar')
    implementation 'androidx.core:core:1.9.0'
}
```

Or alternatively on-line with a Maven repo:
dependencies {
```
    implementation 'org.godotengine:godot:4.4.1.stable'
    implementation 'androidx.core:core:1.9.0'
}
```

Result will be the same..

- Configure similarly in Godot with a plugin.cfg (and export_plugin.gd)
[plugin]
name="TestPluginName"
script="export_plugin.gd"

Observe similar errors:
[MediatorScript] Engine.has_singleton('TestPluginName') is TRUE.
[MediatorScript] SUCCESS: Java plugin 'TestPluginName' instance obtained: <JNISingleton#2835349665>
ERROR: Java plugin instance does NOT have the method 'checkConnection()'.


**Conclusion**
The result is exactly the same:
Plugin is included on Build, and is reported to exist/be found by Godot.
But the Functions/methods contained inside cannot be Called!!

There seems to be a base communication problem between Java Plugins apparently included on Build, and Godot.

- This doesn happe nwith All Plugins tho!

Some Godot plugins are clearly able to do this correctly: (today)
Admob or Appodeal (even tho it’s outdated)

They seem to include their own .aar files on Build, 
and be able to Call/use the functions contained.

But some clearly are Not..

Maybe they use a different/older integration method on build?
Maybe it's a more deep level/native integration with Godot,
that somehow manages to pass whatever layer is preventing our own plugins to operate?

-Maybe there's some Details we're missing?

Since using  this this Godot-Android-Plugin-Template gives the same result, we can rule out my Java code..

Maybe the Godot-Android-Plugin-Template is wrong on a fundamental level?
Maybe this “old” template is not up to date to the latest Godot changes?

Maybe casually this template does the same mistakes I did,
or misses the same Details I missed?


-Anybody has had any success compiling a Java plugin and using it in Godot?
what version of Godot?

Why cannot we Call the functions contained on the Java plugins, if they are included on build?
Could this be a bug in Godot's JNI or plugin system?

What is the correct process to ensure @UsedByGodot methods are callable in Godot 4.4/4.5?
What does Godot 4.4/4.5 need to see, in order to build and integrate Java plugs correctly?

Is the Godot-Android-Plugin-Template outdated or misconfigured for recent Godot versions?

Any ideas??


**Possible Causes**
Naming Convention Issue: 
Despite using exact Java method names (camelCase > helloWorld)  Godot fails to recognize them. 

I thought it could be a snake_case vs. camelCase issue.
But after trying both ways, I guess we can rule out the problem. > The Calls are apparently Correct.

JNI Integration Bug:
Godot's JNI layer may not properly expose @UsedByGodot methods to GDScript.

Documentation Gaps:
Godot's Android plugin documentation:
https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/platform/android/android_plugin.html

May be missing critical steps necessary for proper method exposure.

**Additional Information**
Godot Versions Tested: 4.4.1.stable, 4.5.dev3, 4.5.dev4 (Mono), Godot v4.3.stable.mono.flathub.
Fresh Android Template (or Custom PCK Encrypted)

Environment:
Debian (trixie)
Android SDK: 34 // NDK: 27
Java: 17
Gradle: 8.2 (also tested 8.4)


**Request**
Please could you provide some guidance on making Java plugin methods callable?
Or a basic empty but Working Template that we could follow/part from?

If other users can replicate the same problem, and we confirm it's a bug in Godot 4.4/4.5, 
I guess a fix could be prioritary, as this **Blocks Android development** itself.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

All necessary files are contained on the Godot-Android-Plugin-Template itself:
https://github.com/m4gr3d/Godot-Android-Plugin-Template
